page.layout: One printed page. At the top: the page number 58 at left and an ornamental border. Below it, centred: the title, then the subtitle "Argumentum" heading. The verse follows in two parts, the first with a woodcut initial C, the second after an ornamental rule with a roman initial N. A catchword sits at the right below the last line. No margin notes.

main_text.l: CANTICUM DEBORÆ ET BARACI EX LIBRI Judicum CAP. V.

l.i: CLara Chananæi Regis quum Debo-ra fastus, Et pauco innumeras fregisset milite turmas, Falcatisque acies armatas curribus:& quum Barbaricæ imperium gentis sæuasque secures Rumpens Abramidis paces revocasset ademptas Auspiciis Superum victrix fortissima vates Tale Deo carmen cecinit comitante Baraco.

main_text.l: NVnc est canendum: Nunc sua, Isacides, Reddenda summo gloria Numini: Jovaque victori sonoris Carminibus tribuenda laus est.

l.i: Namque ille vindex fortior hosticas Rupit phalanges: reddidit & Ducum Parere mandatis suorum Abramidas dociles verendis. Audite reges, quos decus aureum

page.notes: The first verse stanza opens with a woodcut initial C; its word is printed "Lara" in small capitals, so it is joined as "CLara". The second stanza opens with a roman initial N with small-capital V. Hyphen in "Debo-ra" is a printed line-end hyphen. The printed "Clarat" at lower right is treated as a catchword. "sæuasque" is read as printed with æ; the word is slightly uncertain on the scan. Ornamental rule and border are not text and are omitted. Faint show-through of the other side is visible at the top right and was left out.
